# Placetta license guides (full text)

Updated 2026-10-21. Source: https://www.placetta.com/guides/. Publisher: Placetta (https://www.placetta.com/about.html). Sourcing policy: https://www.placetta.com/editorial.html. General information, not legal advice; check each agency's page before filing.

## Answers
### How do I get an EIN without an SSN or ITIN?
File Form SS-4 by fax or mail, or call the IRS international line; applying online needs an SSN or ITIN. On line 7b, a responsible party with neither writes "Foreign". By fax it takes about 4 business days, by mail about 4 to 5 weeks. The IRS charges nothing; sites that charge for an EIN are resellers. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/get-an-ein-without-an-ssn.html

### How long does it take to get an EIN?
With an SSN or ITIN, online, it's issued right away. Without one: about 4 business days by fax, about 4 to 5 weeks by mail, and on the call if you phone the IRS international line. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/how-long-does-an-ein-take.html

### Does a foreign-owned single-member LLC have to file Form 5472?
Yes, every year, attached to a pro forma Form 1120 by the tax return due date. It can't be filed electronically for a disregarded entity, and the penalty for not filing starts at $25,000. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/form-5472-foreign-owned-llc.html

### Do I still need to file a beneficial ownership report (BOIR)?
Only if the company was formed outside the US and registered to do business in a US state. Since March 2025, US-formed companies are exempt. It's free, filed online, and due 30 days after the state registration takes effect. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/do-i-need-to-file-a-boir.html

### How do I become an importer of record in the US?
Get an EIN, create your importer identity with CBP Form 5106 (usually through your customs broker), buy a customs bond (CBP Form 301) from a CBP-approved surety, and open an ACE portal account to see your entries, duties and bond. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/become-an-importer-of-record.html

### Does my business need FDA food facility registration?
Yes if it makes, packs or holds food for US consumption, including facilities abroad. Restaurants and retail food stores are exempt. It's free, filed online, and renewed between October 1 and December 31 of every even-numbered year. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/fda-food-facility-registration.html

### Do I need to register cosmetics with the FDA?
Under MoCRA, the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics registers it (Form FDA 5066, every two years), and the brand on the label lists each product (Form FDA 5067, updated every year). Both are free and filed in Cosmetics Direct. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/register-cosmetics-with-the-fda.html

### Do imported consumer products need a certificate of conformity?
Yes, for products covered by CPSC rules. The importer issues the certificate itself; there is no government form. Under the eFiling rule, the certificate data is filed with CBP at entry. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/certificate-of-conformity-for-imports.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in New York City?
Across the 11 filings a restaurant in New York City makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $554.60; 4 more depend on the space or business and 3 are free. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in Los Angeles?
Across the 12 filings a restaurant in Los Angeles makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $890; 6 more depend on the space or business and 3 are free. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/los-angeles-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in Houston?
Across the 13 filings a restaurant in Houston makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $325; 7 more depend on the space or business and 4 are free. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/houston-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### Who needs a Food Protection Certificate in New York City?
Every food service establishment: a certified supervisor must be on site whenever you're open. The course is free online; the exam is taken in person. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-food-protection-certificate.html

### Do I need a seller's permit in California?
Yes, before your first sale, with one permit for each location. Registration is online and free, though CDTFA may ask for a security deposit. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/california-sellers-permit.html

### When do I need a sales tax Certificate of Authority in New York?
Apply through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. It's free, usually takes about two weeks, and the certificate is displayed at each location. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/new-york-certificate-of-authority.html

### Does a foreign company need to register for VAT in the UK?
Yes, from its first UK sale: a business not established in the UK has no threshold. UK-established businesses register once taxable turnover passes £90,000 in 12 months. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/uk-vat-for-foreign-companies.html

### How do I register a food business in the UK?
Register with your local council at least 28 days before opening. It's free; the council inspects and gives a food hygiene rating. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/uk-food-business-registration.html

### How do I get a trade licence in Dubai?
For a mainland business, reserve the trade name, get initial approval, then issue the licence online through Invest in Dubai. Free zone companies license through their own free zone authority instead. It renews every year. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/dubai-trade-licence.html

### Does a foreign company need a MISA license in Saudi Arabia?
Yes. A foreign-owned business gets the investment license from the Ministry of Investment before its commercial registration, and renews it with the commercial registration. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/saudi-arabia-misa-license.html

### How does a foreign company open a business in China?
Register with the local Administration for Market Regulation on the city's one-stop portal, which also sets up tax, social insurance and the company seal. The foreign investment information report goes through the same registration, and the foreign shareholder's documents need notarization and legalization or an apostille. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/open-a-company-in-china-as-a-foreigner.html

### Do I need a food business license in China?
Yes to make or serve food: apply online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead. The license is valid for 5 years. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/china-food-business-license.html

### Does a new California LLC have to pay the $800 tax in its first year?
Yes. Every LLC whose articles are accepted in California, or that does business there, owes the $800 annual tax from its first taxable year, which starts when the Secretary of State files the articles. Pay it with Form FTB 3522 by the 15th day of the 4th month of that year, then every year after. An LLC formed in another state that registers or starts business in California after that date pays right away. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/california-llc-800-tax-first-year.html

### Does a Texas LLC have to file a franchise tax report if it owes no tax?
Yes. Franchise tax applies to every taxable entity formed in Texas or doing business there, and reports are due May 15 each year. Since the 2024 report year there is no No Tax Due Report: an entity with annualized total revenue at or below the no tax due threshold ($2,650,000 for 2026 and 2027 reports) owes nothing but still files a Public Information Report or an Ownership Information Report. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/texas-franchise-tax-no-tax-due.html

### Do I need a sales tax permit in Texas?
Yes if you are engaged in business in Texas and sell, lease or rent taxable goods or provide taxable services. Apply online before your first sale, with one permit for each location. It's free, though the Comptroller may require a security; the permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks and doesn't expire. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/texas-sales-tax-permit.html

### How do I get a restaurant permit in New York City?
Apply for the Health Department's Food Service Establishment Permit online, or in person by appointment; new applications aren't accepted by mail. It costs $280, you need a Food Protection Certificate holder or a course registration when you apply, and you may open 22 days after applying, even before the pre-permit inspection. It renews every year. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-food-service-establishment-permit.html

### How much does a US customs bond cost?
CBP charges nothing for the bond itself (CBP Form 301); you pay a premium to a CBP-approved surety, usually arranged by your customs broker. A continuous bond covers a year of entries with at least $50,000 of coverage and renews yearly. CBP takes at least 5 business days to review it. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/how-much-does-a-customs-bond-cost.html

### Can a Chinese investor get an E-2 visa?
Not as a citizen of the People's Republic of China: the State Department's list of E-1 and E-2 treaty countries doesn't include mainland China or Hong Kong. Taiwan is on the list, as China (Taiwan), for both E-1 and E-2. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/is-china-an-e2-treaty-country.html

### How does a foreign owner get an ITIN?
File Form W-7 with the IRS, generally attached to a US federal tax return unless an exception applies. Mail it with original or certified identity documents, use a Certifying Acceptance Agent, or book an IRS Taxpayer Assistance Center. Allow 7 weeks to hear back. A company doesn't need its owner's ITIN to get an EIN: Form SS-4 works without one. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/how-to-get-an-itin.html

### Does a Chinese company need a US attorney to file a trademark?
Yes. The USPTO requires every applicant domiciled outside the US to be represented by a US-licensed attorney, and every applicant must give and keep current its domicile address. The base application fee is $350 for each class of goods or services. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/us-trademark-for-chinese-companies.html

### Do food shipments from China need FDA Prior Notice?
Yes. Every imported food shipment needs Prior Notice before it arrives: at least 2 hours ahead by road, 4 by rail or air and 8 by water, and before it is sent by international mail. Anyone with the information can submit it, through FDA's system or the customs broker's ABI. Food without proper notice can be refused and held at the port, and food from an unregistered foreign facility can be held until it registers. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/fda-prior-notice-for-food-imports.html

### Is the $800 de minimis exemption still available for imports?
No. Duty-free de minimis ended for goods from China and Hong Kong on May 2, 2025 and for all countries on August 29, 2025. CBP suspended it indefinitely in its regulations on June 24, 2026, so low-value shipments now go through informal or formal entry and pay duty. By law the exemption ends permanently on July 1, 2027. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/de-minimis-800-exemption-status.html

### Does a single-member LLC with no employees need an EIN?
Not for federal tax alone: with no employees and no excise tax, it can use the owner's number. The IRS says most new single-member LLCs still need one, for example to open a bank account or when state tax law requires it. A foreign owner can't apply online and uses Form SS-4 by fax or mail, or the IRS international line. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/does-a-single-member-llc-need-an-ein.html

### Do restaurant workers in California need a food handler card?
Yes. Food workers who prepare, store or handle food must get a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of being hired, from an ANSI-accredited course. The card is valid for three years. Workers who hold a valid food safety certification are exempt. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/california-food-handler-card.html

### Can a foreigner form an LLC in Texas?
Yes. Texas law doesn't restrict who can form or own a business entity, so you don't need to be a US citizen or resident; the organizer only has to be a person capable of entering into a contract. The LLC files Form 205 with the Secretary of State. https://www.placetta.com/guides/answers/can-a-foreigner-form-a-texas-llc.html

## City guides
### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in New York City
https://www.placetta.com/guides/new-york-city/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in New York City takes 11 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (New York LLC) and ending with the sign permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $554.60, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (New York LLC), New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Filed online with the Department of State, or mailed. Fee: $200. Takes: A few business days online; expedite is extra. https://dos.ny.gov/limited-liability-company-articles-organization
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. LLC publication within 120 days, New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Publish a notice in two newspapers chosen by the county clerk for six weeks, then file the certificate with the affidavits. Fee: $50. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited processing within 24 hours ($25). https://dos.ny.gov/certificate-publication-domestic-limited-liability-company-0
4. Certificate of Occupancy for the use, NYC Department of Buildings. Check the space's existing CO allows your use; a change of use needs an alteration filing and an amended CO. Fee: Varies. Takes: DOB doesn't publish a processing time for a Certificate of Occupancy; staff review the request in DOB NOW: Build and issue the CO once every sign-off and requirement is in. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/certificate-of-occupancy.page
5. Application for Registration as a Sales Tax Vendor (Certificate of Authority), New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Apply online through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. Display the certificate at each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually about two weeks. https://www.businessexpress.ny.gov/
6. Building permit for the build-out (DOB alteration), NYC Department of Buildings. Department of Buildings work permits are required for most construction; a registered design professional (PE or RA) files the alteration in DOB NOW: Build, and a change of use also amends the Certificate of Occupancy. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-build-resources-laa.page
7. New employer registration for unemployment insurance and withholding, New York State Department of Labor. Register online once you pay wages in New York. Fee: Free. Takes: The Department of Labor doesn't publish how long registration takes; it assigns each liable employer an eight-digit employer registration number after you register. https://dol.ny.gov/register-unemployment-insurance-0
8. Proof of workers' comp and disability/paid family leave insurance, New York State Workers' Compensation Board. Buy the policies from an insurer; the insurer reports coverage to the Board. Agencies ask for the certificates. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Board doesn't publish a processing time because coverage is bought from an insurer, but DB/PFL coverage must be in place within four weeks after a new employee's 30th day of work. https://www.wcb.ny.gov/content/main/coverage-requirements.jsp
9. Food Protection Certificate (course and exam), NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Free online course, then an in-person exam. A certified supervisor must be on site whenever you are open. Fee: $24.60. Takes: Certificate arrives 2 to 6 weeks after the exam. https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/business/health-academy/food-protection-online-free.page
10. Food Service Establishment Permit, NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Apply on NYC Business. The Health Department inspects before issuing; letter grades follow. Fee: $280. Takes: You may open 22 days after applying, even before the pre-permit inspection. https://nyc-business.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/description/food-service-establishment-permit
11. Sign permit, NYC Department of Buildings. Filed in DOB NOW by a registered design professional or licensed sign hanger. Fee: Varies. Takes: DOB doesn't publish a review time for sign permits; the sign permit is filed in DOB NOW: Build, with a separate electrical permit if the sign is lit. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/sign-permit.page
What's different for a milk tea shop in New York City:
- New York City requires a grease interceptor of a business that produces and disposes of fat, oil or grease; its examples are restaurants and food processing establishments. Whether your shop needs one turns on what its kitchen makes, and a licensed plumber sizes it. NYC Department of Environmental Protection: "like a restaurant, food processing establishment, hospital or day care and senior center, you need a grease interceptor." https://ht.nyc-business.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/description/grease-interceptor-information (read 2026-10-21)

### Retail stores in New York City
https://www.placetta.com/guides/new-york-city/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in New York City takes 8 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (New York LLC) and ending with the sign permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $250, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores.

Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited processing within 24 hours ($25). https://dos.ny.gov/certificate-publication-domestic-limited-liability-company-0
4. Certificate of Occupancy for the use, NYC Department of Buildings. Check the space's existing CO allows your use; a change of use needs an alteration filing and an amended CO. Fee: Varies. Takes: DOB doesn't publish a processing time for a Certificate of Occupancy; staff review the request in DOB NOW: Build and issue the CO once every sign-off and requirement is in. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/certificate-of-occupancy.page
5. Application for Registration as a Sales Tax Vendor (Certificate of Authority), New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Apply online through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. Display the certificate at each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually about two weeks. https://www.businessexpress.ny.gov/
6. New employer registration for unemployment insurance and withholding, New York State Department of Labor. Register online once you pay wages in New York. Fee: Free. Takes: The Department of Labor doesn't publish how long registration takes; it assigns each liable employer an eight-digit employer registration number after you register. https://dol.ny.gov/register-unemployment-insurance-0
7. Proof of workers' comp and disability/paid family leave insurance, New York State Workers' Compensation Board. Buy the policies from an insurer; the insurer reports coverage to the Board. Agencies ask for the certificates. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Board doesn't publish a processing time because coverage is bought from an insurer, but DB/PFL coverage must be in place within four weeks after a new employee's 30th day of work. https://www.wcb.ny.gov/content/main/coverage-requirements.jsp
8. Sign permit, NYC Department of Buildings. Filed in DOB NOW by a registered design professional or licensed sign hanger. Fee: Varies. Takes: DOB doesn't publish a review time for sign permits; the sign permit is filed in DOB NOW: Build, with a separate electrical permit if the sign is lit. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/sign-permit.page

10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Los Angeles
https://www.placetta.com/guides/los-angeles/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Los Angeles takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. City of Los Angeles business tax registration, City of Los Angeles Office of Finance. Register online within 30 days of starting business in the city. Fee: Varies. Takes: Temporary certificate issued immediately; permanent one mailed in 4 to 6 weeks. https://finance.lacity.gov/register-new-business
6. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
7. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
8. Food facility plan check, Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Submit plans before building out; approval comes before the public health permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review within 20 working days. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/i-want-to/submit-electronic-plan.htm
9. Building permit and Certificate of Occupancy, Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety. Tenant improvements and changes of use go through plan check; a new use gets a new Certificate of Occupancy. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plans are returned within weeks, depending on workload. https://dbs.lacity.gov/services/plan-review-permitting/building-permits
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. Public health permit (food facility), Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Apply after plan approval and before opening; an inspector visits first. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review is completed within 20 working days after payment (10 if you pay for expedited review); the inspector needs at least 3 working days' notice for the final inspection, and the permit is issued after the permit fee is paid. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/docs/permit/Public-Health-Permit-License-Application.pdf
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in Los Angeles:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)

6. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
7. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
8. Food facility plan check, Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Submit plans before building out; approval comes before the public health permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review within 20 working days. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/i-want-to/submit-electronic-plan.htm
9. Building permit and Certificate of Occupancy, Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety. Tenant improvements and changes of use go through plan check; a new use gets a new Certificate of Occupancy. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plans are returned within weeks, depending on workload. https://dbs.lacity.gov/services/plan-review-permitting/building-permits
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. Public health permit (food facility), Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Apply after plan approval and before opening; an inspector visits first. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plan review is completed within 20 working days after payment (10 if you pay for expedited review); the inspector needs at least 3 working days' notice for the final inspection, and the permit is issued after the permit fee is paid. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/docs/permit/Public-Health-Permit-License-Application.pdf
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in Los Angeles:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Retail stores in Los Angeles
https://www.placetta.com/guides/los-angeles/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in Los Angeles takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 1 fee is set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. City of Los Angeles business tax registration, City of Los Angeles Office of Finance. Register online within 30 days of starting business in the city. Fee: Varies. Takes: Temporary certificate issued immediately; permanent one mailed in 4 to 6 weeks. https://finance.lacity.gov/register-new-business
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
8. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Cosmetics stores in Los Angeles
https://www.placetta.com/guides/los-angeles/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Los Angeles takes 14 filings with 11 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 8 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Takes: Temporary certificate issued immediately; permanent one mailed in 4 to 6 weeks. https://finance.lacity.gov/register-new-business
6. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
7. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
8. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
11. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
13. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
14. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Restaurants in Houston
https://www.placetta.com/guides/houston/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Houston takes 13 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Food establishment plan review, Houston Health Department. Submit plans before building or remodeling a food establishment. Fee: Varies. Takes: No standard time published; expedited review in 1 to 2 business days. https://www.houstonhealth.org/food-permits/opening-food-establishment
8. Buildout permit (building permit for the space), City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. For building out empty space in a commercial building: plan review and inspections, with the Fire Marshal and the Health Department reviewing where the work calls for it. The permit stays on site until final approval. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1148
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. Form CE-1045-A, emailed to Occupancy Inspections (Occupancy.Inspections@houstontx.gov); iPermits is only for paying afterwards. Needed for a new tenant use or change of use inside city limits. Fee: Varies. Takes: Houston lists the Certificate of Occupancy's processing time as 15 minutes once the final inspection is approved; the certificate is emailed to you. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1106
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
11. Food dealer permit, Houston Health Department. The operating permit, issued after plan review and inspection. The application is emailed to Food-COO@houstontx.gov. Fee: Varies. Takes: Up to 15 business days. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hhd1003
12. Sign permit, City of Houston, Sign Administration. Filed with the Houston Permitting Center before the sign goes up. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 4 to 11 business days. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1112
13. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Food establishment plan review, Houston Health Department. Submit plans before building or remodeling a food establishment. Fee: Varies. Takes: No standard time published; expedited review in 1 to 2 business days. https://www.houstonhealth.org/food-permits/opening-food-establishment
8. Buildout permit (building permit for the space), City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. For building out empty space in a commercial building: plan review and inspections, with the Fire Marshal and the Health Department reviewing where the work calls for it. The permit stays on site until final approval. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1148
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. Form CE-1045-A, emailed to Occupancy Inspections (Occupancy.Inspections@houstontx.gov); iPermits is only for paying afterwards. Needed for a new tenant use or change of use inside city limits. Fee: Varies. Takes: Houston lists the Certificate of Occupancy's processing time as 15 minutes once the final inspection is approved; the certificate is emailed to you. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1106
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
11. Food dealer permit, Houston Health Department. The operating permit, issued after plan review and inspection. The application is emailed to Food-COO@houstontx.gov. Fee: Varies. Takes: Up to 15 business days. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hhd1003
12. Sign permit, City of Houston, Sign Administration. Filed with the Houston Permitting Center before the sign goes up. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 4 to 11 business days. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1112
13. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/
What's different for a bakery in Houston:
- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Restaurants in Beijing
https://www.placetta.com/guides/beijing/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Beijing takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company registration and business license and ending with the fire safety check before opening. None of them has a fixed government fee and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually 1 to 3 business days once the documents are complete. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Beijing's one-stop portal, Beijing e-Window (e窗通). Beijing's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://ect.scjgj.beijing.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually the same day online. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

None of them has a fixed government fee and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually 1 to 3 business days once the documents are complete. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Beijing's one-stop portal, Beijing e-Window (e窗通). Beijing's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://ect.scjgj.beijing.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually the same day online. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Customs registration for importers and exporters, General Administration of Customs. Filed online through the China International Trade Single Window. The separate foreign trade operator filing was abolished in 2022. Fee: Free. https://www.singlewindow.cn

### Restaurants in Shanghai
https://www.placetta.com/guides/shanghai/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Shanghai takes 6 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the company registration and business license and ending with the fire safety check before opening. None of them has a fixed government fee and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually 1 to 3 business days once the documents are complete. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Shanghai's one-stop portal, Shanghai One-Window business portal (一窗通). Shanghai's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://yct.sh.gov.cn

4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

Opening a retail store in Hangzhou takes 5 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the company registration and business license and ending with the fire safety check before opening. None of them has a fixed government fee and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually 1 to 3 business days once the documents are complete. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Hangzhou's one-stop portal, Zhejiang Government Services (浙里办). Hangzhou's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://www.zjzwfw.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually the same day online. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually 1 to 3 business days once the documents are complete. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Wuhan's one-stop portal, Hubei Government Services. Wuhan's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://zwfw.hubei.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually the same day online. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Customs registration for importers and exporters, General Administration of Customs. Filed online through the China International Trade Single Window. The separate foreign trade operator filing was abolished in 2022. Fee: Free. https://www.singlewindow.cn

6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

### Retail stores in Xi'an
https://www.placetta.com/guides/xi-an/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in Xi'an takes 5 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the company registration and business license and ending with the fire safety check before opening. None of them has a fixed government fee and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually 1 to 3 business days once the documents are complete. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Xi'an's one-stop portal, Shaanxi Government Services. Xi'an's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://zwfw.shaanxi.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. Takes: Usually the same day online. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

### Restaurants in London
https://www.placetta.com/guides/london/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in London takes 5 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the company incorporation and ending with the premises licence (alcohol or late-night hot food). None of them has a fixed government fee, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company incorporation, Companies House. Filed online with Companies House. Every director and person with significant control must verify their identity first. Fee: Varies. Takes: Online applications are usually done within 24 hours. https://www.gov.uk/limited-company-formation/register-your-company
2. VAT registration, HM Revenue & Customs. Required once taxable turnover passes £90,000 in 12 months. A business not established in the UK registers from its first UK sale. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/register-for-vat
3. Employer registration (PAYE), HM Revenue & Customs. Register before the first payday; it can take up to 5 working days to get the employer reference. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/register-employer
4. Food business registration, Local council environmental health. Register with the local council at least 28 days before opening. It's free, and the council inspects and gives a food hygiene rating. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/food-business-registration
5. Premises licence (alcohol or late-night hot food), Local council licensing. Needed only to sell alcohol, or hot food and drink between 11pm and 5am. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.uk/premises-licence

### Restaurants in Paris
https://www.placetta.com/guides/paris/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Paris takes 3 filings with 3 agencies, starting with the company creation (one-stop formalities portal) and ending with the food establishment declaration. None of them has a fixed government fee, 1 fee is set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Company creation (one-stop formalities portal), INPI, Guichet unique. All company creations are filed online here; the registration gives the SIREN and SIRET numbers and the intra-EU VAT number follows from the tax office. Fee: Varies. https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
2. Business tax account and VAT, Direction générale des Finances publiques. Open the professional space to file and pay VAT and business taxes online. Fee: Free. https://www.impots.gouv.fr/professionnel
3. Food establishment declaration, Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP). Declared online before opening, for any business that prepares, handles or stores food of animal origin. Fee: Free. https://mesdemarches.agriculture.gouv.fr

### Importers and online sellers in Paris
https://www.placetta.com/guides/paris/importer-ecommerce.html

3. EORI number for importing, Direction générale des douanes. Requested online from French customs before the first import. Fee: Free. https://www.douane.gouv.fr

### Restaurants in Berlin
https://www.placetta.com/guides/berlin/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Berlin takes 4 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the commercial register entry (GmbH) and ending with the tax registration questionnaire. None of them has a fixed government fee, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to retail stores, grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Commercial register entry (GmbH), Local court (Registergericht), through a notary. The articles are notarized and the notary files the registration electronically. Fee: Varies. https://www.handelsregister.de
2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Bundesanzeiger Verlag, Transparency Register. Companies record their beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration, Bezirksamt Berlin, Ordnungsamt. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with Berlin before starting. The city passes it on to the tax office and the food inspectors. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/121921/
4. Tax registration questionnaire, Finanzamt (through ELSTER). Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then issues the tax number and VAT ID. Fee: Free. https://www.elster.de

### Importers and online sellers in Berlin
https://www.placetta.com/guides/berlin/importer-ecommerce.html

4. Tax registration questionnaire, Finanzamt (through ELSTER). Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then issues the tax number and VAT ID. Fee: Free. https://www.elster.de
5. EORI number for importing, German customs (Zoll). Requested from German customs before the first import. Fee: Free. https://www.zoll.de

### Restaurants in Madrid

Opening a restaurant in Madrid takes 4 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the company creation (CIRCE) and ending with the opening licence or responsible declaration. None of them has a fixed government fee, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to retail stores, grocery stores, cosmetics stores, toy stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.

2. Tax census declaration, Agencia Tributaria. Registers the business for VAT and income tax before it starts trading. Fee: Free. https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
3. Employer registration with Social Security, Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social. Register as an employer and sign up each worker before they start. Fee: Free. https://sede.seg-social.gob.es
4. Opening licence or responsible declaration, Ayuntamiento de Madrid. Most shops and restaurants open with a responsible declaration filed online; larger works need a licence. Fee: Varies. https://sede.madrid.es

### Restaurants in Dubai
https://www.placetta.com/guides/dubai/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Dubai takes 4 filings with 4 agencies, starting with the dubai trade licence and ending with the food establishment approval. None of them has a fixed government fee, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores, milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. Dubai trade licence, Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. Reserve the trade name, get initial approval, then issue the licence online through Invest in Dubai. Free zones license through their own authority instead. Fee: Varies. https://invest.dubai.ae
2. Corporate tax and VAT registration, Federal Tax Authority. Every company registers for corporate tax on EmaraTax. VAT registration is required once taxable supplies pass AED 375,000 a year. Fee: Free. https://eservices.tax.gov.ae
3. Employer registration and work permits, Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Register the establishment, then apply for each employee's work permit. Fee: Varies. https://www.mohre.gov.ae
4. Food establishment approval, Dubai Municipality, Food Safety. Food businesses get the municipality's layout approval and inspection before the licence is activated. Fee: Varies. https://www.dm.gov.ae

None of them has a fixed government fee, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. 3. Tax, VAT and zakat registration, Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA). Register for zakat or income tax, and for VAT once taxable supplies pass SAR 375,000 a year. E-invoicing applies. Fee: Free. https://zatca.gov.sa
4. Social insurance employer registration, General Organization for Social Insurance. Register as an employer and enroll each employee. Fee: Free. https://www.gosi.gov.sa
5. Municipal license, Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Housing (Balady). Every shop, restaurant and warehouse gets the municipal license for its premises online. Fee: Varies. https://balady.gov.sa
6. Civil Defense safety license, General Directorate of Civil Defense. Premises open to the public and warehouses get the safety license online. Fee: Varies. https://998.gov.sa

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Francisco
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in San Francisco takes 15 filings with 11 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $4,068, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. Takes: The certificate is mailed within 10 to 15 business days after payment. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application
8. Formula retail (chain store) affidavit, San Francisco Planning Department. A chain with 11 or more other locations worldwide files this with the building permit. Many neighborhood districts then require a Conditional Use hearing, and a few ban chains. Fee: Varies. Takes: The affidavit itself isn't reviewed separately, but where neighborhood notification is required, neighbors get 30 days to respond, and districts that need Conditional Use go to a Planning Commission hearing. https://sfplanning.org/resource/formula-retail-establishments
9. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
10. Food facility plan check, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Filed with the building permit at the Permit Center, with health as a review station: the application, plans and the review fee. Fee: $2,207. Takes: DPH doesn't publish a plan review time, but asks you to contact your plan reviewer at least 2 weeks ahead to book the pre-final and final site inspections. https://sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-07/PlanCheckApplication.pdf
11. Building permit for a tenant improvement, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Submit plans and the application at the Permit Center, which routes it to Planning, Fire and Health. Fee: Varies. Takes: Eligible small businesses opening a new business can get a 30-day review once the application is complete. https://www.sf.gov/step-by-step--get-otc-permit-your-commercial-project/
12. Health permit to operate a food facility, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Apply online at least six weeks before opening, with your business account, location ID and federal tax ID, once a certified food safety manager is on staff. Fee: $470. Takes: Apply for the health permit at least 1 month before you open. https://sf.gov/get-health-permit-open-restaurant-bar-or-other-retail-food-location
13. Sign and awning permit, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Online only through PermitSF since June 29, 2026 (Forms 4 and 7 retired): submit drawings, answer plan review, pay, then book the final inspection. Lit signs also need an electrical permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: DBI doesn't publish a review time for sign or awning permits; you apply online with construction drawings, and the sign must meet the zoning rules for your district. https://sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning
14. Fire Department place of assembly permit, San Francisco Fire Department. For dining rooms above the assembly occupant load: file with the Fire Prevention permits section, which inspects before issuing. Fee: $446. Takes: Fire permit applications must be submitted at least 5 working days before the activity or operation starts. https://sf-fire.org/permits
15. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in San Francisco:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)

- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Cosmetics stores in San Francisco
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in San Francisco takes 16 filings with 13 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $945, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 8 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/

4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. Takes: The certificate is mailed within 10 to 15 business days after payment. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application
11. Formula retail (chain store) affidavit, San Francisco Planning Department. A chain with 11 or more other locations worldwide files this with the building permit. Many neighborhood districts then require a Conditional Use hearing, and a few ban chains. Fee: Varies. Takes: The affidavit itself isn't reviewed separately, but where neighborhood notification is required, neighbors get 30 days to respond, and districts that need Conditional Use go to a Planning Commission hearing. https://sfplanning.org/resource/formula-retail-establishments
12. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
13. Sign and awning permit, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Online only through PermitSF since June 29, 2026 (Forms 4 and 7 retired): submit drawings, answer plan review, pay, then book the final inspection. Lit signs also need an electrical permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: DBI doesn't publish a review time for sign or awning permits; you apply online with construction drawings, and the sign must meet the zoning rules for your district. https://sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning
14. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
15. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
16. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses
