### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Jose
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-jose/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in San Jose takes 15 filings with 11 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $1,335, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of San José Business Tax Certificate, City of San José Finance Department. Register online within 90 days of starting business in San José, with the owner, tax ID, location and, if you have them, the seller's permit and county health permit numbers. Fee: Varies. Takes: If you pay during registration, the account activates in 2 to 3 business days; otherwise the invoice is mailed within 5 to 10 business days. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/finance/business-tax-registration/register-for-a-business-tax-certificate
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Email the application, scaled plans, menu and equipment sheets to dehplancheck@deh.sccgov.org, then pay the invoiced review fee. The city needs the county's stamped plans before its own plan check. Fee: Varies. Takes: After payment, inspector review may take up to 20 business days. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
10. Building permit for a tenant improvement, City of San José Building Division. Apply on SJPermits.org, upload plans through SJePlans and pay the plan review fee before review starts. Restaurants can use the city's Streamlined Restaurant Program. Fee: Varies. Takes: San José's standard plan review for a commercial tenant improvement takes about 10 working days for the first round and 5 working days for each recheck. https://www.sjpermits.org
11. Fire protection system permit, San José Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention. When plan check calls for it, apply on SJPermits.org under Fire Prevention, pay, then upload documents in SJePlans. Fee: Varies. Takes: Fire Department review of fire protection system plans takes about 10 working days for the first round and 5 working days for each recheck on a commercial project. https://www.sjpermits.org
12. Building final inspection, City of San José Building Division. Schedule the final on SJPermits.org once every other inspection on the permit has passed. Fee: Varies. Takes: San José doesn't publish a wait time for the final inspection; you request it on SJPermits.org, and it's approved only after every other inspection on the permit has passed. https://www.sjpermits.org
13. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
14. Sign permit, City of San José Planning Division. Upload the signed application to SJPermits.org, then pay the invoice. Fee: $445. Takes: Average: 2 weeks. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/business/development-services-permit-center/online-permits-at-sjpermits-org/planning-online-permits
15. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in San Jose:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)

4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of San José Business Tax Certificate, City of San José Finance Department. Register online within 90 days of starting business in San José, with the owner, tax ID, location and, if you have them, the seller's permit and county health permit numbers. Fee: Varies. Takes: If you pay during registration, the account activates in 2 to 3 business days; otherwise the invoice is mailed within 5 to 10 business days. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/finance/business-tax-registration/register-for-a-business-tax-certificate
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Email the application, scaled plans, menu and equipment sheets to dehplancheck@deh.sccgov.org, then pay the invoiced review fee. The city needs the county's stamped plans before its own plan check. Fee: Varies. Takes: After payment, inspector review may take up to 20 business days. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
10. Building permit for a tenant improvement, City of San José Building Division. Apply on SJPermits.org, upload plans through SJePlans and pay the plan review fee before review starts. Restaurants can use the city's Streamlined Restaurant Program. Fee: Varies. Takes: San José's standard plan review for a commercial tenant improvement takes about 10 working days for the first round and 5 working days for each recheck. https://www.sjpermits.org
11. Fire protection system permit, San José Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention. When plan check calls for it, apply on SJPermits.org under Fire Prevention, pay, then upload documents in SJePlans. Fee: Varies. Takes: Fire Department review of fire protection system plans takes about 10 working days for the first round and 5 working days for each recheck on a commercial project. https://www.sjpermits.org
12. Building final inspection, City of San José Building Division. Schedule the final on SJPermits.org once every other inspection on the permit has passed. Fee: Varies. Takes: San José doesn't publish a wait time for the final inspection; you request it on SJPermits.org, and it's approved only after every other inspection on the permit has passed. https://www.sjpermits.org
13. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
14. Sign permit, City of San José Planning Division. Upload the signed application to SJPermits.org, then pay the invoice. Fee: $445. Takes: Average: 2 weeks. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/business/development-services-permit-center/online-permits-at-sjpermits-org/planning-online-permits
15. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in San Jose:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Grocery stores in San Jose
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-jose/grocery-store.html
Opening a grocery store in San Jose takes 10 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $1,335, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. City of San José Business Tax Certificate, City of San José Finance Department. Register online within 90 days of starting business in San José, with the owner, tax ID, location and, if you have them, the seller's permit and county health permit numbers. Fee: Varies. Takes: If you pay during registration, the account activates in 2 to 3 business days; otherwise the invoice is mailed within 5 to 10 business days. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/finance/business-tax-registration/register-for-a-business-tax-certificate
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county's plan review can take up to 20 business days, and the invoice for the operating permit is sent after the final inspection passes. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
8. Sign permit, City of San José Planning Division. Upload the signed application to SJPermits.org, then pay the invoice. Fee: $445. Takes: Average: 2 weeks. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/business/development-services-permit-center/online-permits-at-sjpermits-org/planning-online-permits
9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
10. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. City of San José Business Tax Certificate, City of San José Finance Department. Register online within 90 days of starting business in San José, with the owner, tax ID, location and, if you have them, the seller's permit and county health permit numbers. Fee: Varies. Takes: If you pay during registration, the account activates in 2 to 3 business days; otherwise the invoice is mailed within 5 to 10 business days. https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/departments-offices/finance/business-tax-registration/register-for-a-business-tax-certificate
9. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Restaurants in Chicago
https://www.placetta.com/guides/chicago/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Chicago takes 8 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the chicago retail food establishment license. The fixed government fees add up to about $150, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Illinois Secretary of State. Form the LLC online, or register a company formed in another state to do business in Illinois. Fee: $150. https://www.ilsos.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Illinois business registration (sales tax), Illinois Department of Revenue. Register before your first purchase, sale or hire: online in MyTax Illinois (Register a New Business, Form REG-1), by mail or at an IDOR office. You get a certificate of registration and a taxpayer ID; Chicago's food license application asks for the Illinois Business Tax number. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 1 to 2 business days online; 4 to 6 weeks on paper. https://mytax.illinois.gov/
4. Chicago food service sanitation certificate, Chicago Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. A person in charge holding this Public Health certificate must be on site whenever food that needs temperature control is prepared, held or served. Pass an approved course, or apply for reciprocity with a valid ANSI-accredited food protection manager certificate. A place selling only prepackaged food doesn't need one. Fee: Varies. https://chicago.gov/city/en/depts/cdph/provdrs/food_safety/svcs/enroll_in_a_foodsanitationcertificationcourse.html
5. Building permit for the interior alteration, Chicago Department of Buildings. Nonstructural interior alterations up to 2,000 square feet can use the Express Permit Program. Fee: Varies. https://chicago.gov/city/en/sites/guide-to-building-permits/home/instructions/EPP/INTWK-alteration.html
6. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Illinois Department of Employment Security. A new business registers with IDES within 30 days of starting, online through MyTax Illinois or on the paper REG-UI-1 form. Fee: Varies. https://mytax.illinois.gov/
7. Food establishment plan review, Chicago Department of Public Health, with the Department of Buildings. For new construction or a rehab, a city health sanitarian reviews the plans as part of the building permit application, coordinated between Public Health and Buildings. Public Health isn't on E-Plan and doesn't review plans filed under the self-certification program. Fee: Varies. https://www.chicago.gov/content/dam/city/depts/bacp/general/Retail%20Food%20Guide.pdf
8. Chicago retail food establishment license, City of Chicago, Business Affairs and Consumer Protection, with the Department of Public Health. Chicago's business license for any fixed place that serves, stores or sells perishable food, at a properly zoned, non-residential address. Apply online or at the Small Business Center, City Hall, 121 N. LaSalle St., Room 800, with the lease, Illinois Business Tax number, FEIN, ownership details and photo ID; the place must pass a public health inspection before the license is issued. Fee: Varies. Takes: Chicago doesn't publish a standard processing time; the license is issued after zoning approval, payment and any required inspections, then mailed to your business. https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/bacp/supp_info/retailfoodestablishment0.html

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Seattle
https://www.placetta.com/guides/seattle/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Seattle takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service business permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $83, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Washington business license (state tax registration), Washington Department of Revenue, Business Licensing Service. File online in My DOR, or by mail. It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Food worker cards for staff, Washington State Department of Health, with local health departments. Everyone who works with unpackaged food, food equipment or utensils takes the state training and exam, online only at foodworkercard.wa.gov or through a local health department. A new worker may start before getting the card, for up to 14 days, if the employer gives food safety training. Fee: $10. https://www.foodworkercard.wa.gov
5. Seattle business license tax certificate, City of Seattle Finance, License and Tax Administration. Apply online through FileLocal once the business has its Washington UBI number, or mail the paper application with payment. A physical business location is required; a P.O. box doesn't count. Fee: $73. Takes: Online, the license can usually be printed 2 to 3 business days after payment; by mail it takes one to six weeks. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx
6. Food establishment plan review, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Plans are reviewed before construction, remodeling or a change of owner. Apply and pay in the Public Health Permit Center with the site plan, menu, floor plan, equipment list with make and model, the plan review questionnaire, the finish schedule and the seating layout. Fee: Varies. Takes: An initial review may take up to 8 to 10 weeks at current volumes. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-plan-review
7. Construction permit for the tenant improvement, Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections. Land use, construction and trade permits for the space come from SDCI; final inspections are scheduled once every permit is approved and the work is done. Fee: Varies. https://www.seattle.gov/sdci
8. Food service business permit, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Once plan review is approved, submit the application to operate in the Public Health Permit Center, pay the operating fee and book the pre-operational inspection at least a week before opening. Opening without that inspection can mean closure and a fee of half the yearly permit. Every employee needs a Washington food worker card. Fee: Varies. Takes: Book the pre-operational inspection at least 1 week before opening. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-business-permit
What's different for a milk tea shop in Seattle:
- King County sets the risk category by the menu: drinks made only from commercially packaged products are Category 1 (low), but using Time as a Public Health Control, holding a food out of temperature control for a set time, makes it Category 3 (high), with two routine inspections a year. Public Health – Seattle & King County: "Using Time as a Public Health Control" https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dph/documents/certificates-permits-licenses/food-worker-business-permits/permanent-businesses/food-establishment-risk-levels.pdf?rev=fa5058bfe2344c0da374012f74cac082&hash=6343EB80E0FD05EB643F9899D4DA212D (read 2026-10-21)

### Coffee shops in Seattle
https://www.placetta.com/guides/seattle/coffee-shop.html
Opening a coffee shop in Seattle takes 8 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service business permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $83, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Washington business license (state tax registration), Washington Department of Revenue, Business Licensing Service. File online in My DOR, or by mail. It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Food worker cards for staff, Washington State Department of Health, with local health departments. Everyone who works with unpackaged food, food equipment or utensils takes the state training and exam, online only at foodworkercard.wa.gov or through a local health department. A new worker may start before getting the card, for up to 14 days, if the employer gives food safety training. Fee: $10. https://www.foodworkercard.wa.gov
5. Seattle business license tax certificate, City of Seattle Finance, License and Tax Administration. Apply online through FileLocal once the business has its Washington UBI number, or mail the paper application with payment. A physical business location is required; a P.O. box doesn't count. Fee: $73. Takes: Online, the license can usually be printed 2 to 3 business days after payment; by mail it takes one to six weeks. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx
6. Food establishment plan review, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Plans are reviewed before construction, remodeling or a change of owner. Apply and pay in the Public Health Permit Center with the site plan, menu, floor plan, equipment list with make and model, the plan review questionnaire, the finish schedule and the seating layout. Fee: Varies. Takes: An initial review may take up to 8 to 10 weeks at current volumes. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-plan-review
7. Construction permit for the tenant improvement, Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections. Land use, construction and trade permits for the space come from SDCI; final inspections are scheduled once every permit is approved and the work is done. Fee: Varies. https://www.seattle.gov/sdci
8. Food service business permit, Public Health, Seattle and King County. Once plan review is approved, submit the application to operate in the Public Health Permit Center, pay the operating fee and book the pre-operational inspection at least a week before opening. Opening without that inspection can mean closure and a fee of half the yearly permit. Every employee needs a Washington food worker card. Fee: Varies. Takes: Book the pre-operational inspection at least 1 week before opening. https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph/certificates-permits-licenses/food-business-permits/permanent-food-business-permit
What's different for a coffee shop in Seattle:
- King County puts a coffee shop in risk Category 1 (low), with one routine inspection a year, when it prepares espresso and blended drinks from commercially packaged products. Cooking or baking on site moves it up a category. Public Health – Seattle & King County: "Scooping ice cream, preparing espresso and/or blended drinks with commercially packaged products." https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dph/documents/certificates-permits-licenses/food-worker-business-permits/permanent-businesses/food-establishment-risk-levels.pdf?rev=fa5058bfe2344c0da374012f74cac082&hash=6343EB80E0FD05EB643F9899D4DA212D (read 2026-10-21)

### Cosmetics stores in Seattle

Opening a cosmetics store in Seattle takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the seattle business license tax certificate. The fixed government fees add up to about $73, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Washington business license (state tax registration), Washington Department of Revenue, Business Licensing Service. File online in My DOR, or by mail. It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Seattle business license tax certificate, City of Seattle Finance, License and Tax Administration. Apply online through FileLocal once the business has its Washington UBI number, or mail the paper application with payment. A physical business location is required; a P.O. box doesn't count. Fee: $73. Takes: Online, the license can usually be printed 2 to 3 business days after payment; by mail it takes one to six weeks. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx

8. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/

### Restaurants in Boston
https://www.placetta.com/guides/boston/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Boston takes 13 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $565, 8 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $500. https://www.sec.state.ma.us
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Sales tax registration, Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Register for sales tax and withholding before trading. Fee: Free. Takes: DOR doesn't publish how long registration takes; once approved, it mails a registration certificate for each location. https://mtc.dor.state.ma.us
4. Certified food protection manager, Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. At least one manager on staff passes a food protection manager exam from a nationally accredited provider that Massachusetts accepts; a backup person in charge covers when they're away. Boston asks for the certificate with the food service permit application. Fee: Varies. https://www.mass.gov/doc/massachusetts-food-protection-manager-certification-exam-and-trainer-directory-1/download
5. Allergen awareness certificate, Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. The person in charge, who must be on site whenever the place is open, and the backup who covers for them take an allergen awareness course and train the staff. Places that cook, prepare or serve food to eat right away need it; Boston asks for the certificate before the opening inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.mass.gov/lists/food-allergen-awareness-guidance
6. Boston business certificate (DBA), City of Boston, City Clerk. Needed when the business trades under a name other than its legal name. Bring the notarized form, the signed lease and photo ID to City Hall, Room 601 (the clerk notarizes free), or mail them with a check; there is no online filing. An LLC or corporation registers with the Secretary of the Commonwealth first. Fee: $65. Takes: Issued while you wait in person; 2 to 3 business days by mail. https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2025/03/2025-New-Business-Certificate-Form_0.pdf
7. Employer registration for unemployment insurance, Massachusetts Department of Unemployment Assistance. Employers who pay wages for work done in Massachusetts register with DUA online: open Unemployment Services for Employers without logging in and choose Register your Business. Fee: Free. https://www.mass.gov/how-to/register-a-business-with-the-department-of-unemployment-assistance
8. Food establishment plan review, City of Boston Inspectional Services, Health Division. Needed to build a new place, renovate, change the layout, or add equipment or processes the menu calls for. Book the in-person review with ISD Health (617-635-5326, ISDHealth@boston.gov) and bring the worksheet, two scaled floor plans, NSF or UL equipment specs and the menu; then take the stamped plans to ISD's Building Division for the building permits. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2021/05/FSPLAN%20REVIEW%20fillable%205%2013%20FINAL.pdf
9. Building permit for the build-out, City of Boston Inspectional Services. A Long Form permit for major construction or structural change, a Short Form for minor work; only licensed contractors apply. The health plan review comes first, and the building, plumbing, gas, electrical and mechanical permits follow it. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/departments/inspectional-services
10. Common Victualler License, City of Boston Licensing Board. Needed to sell food made to order at a fixed place, seated or takeout. File on the Licensing Board's online form with the lease, a floor plan, each owner's personal information form and the wage theft form, once the Certificate of Occupancy is in hand. A new address, or hours outside 6 a.m. to 11 p.m., goes to a public hearing after the neighborhood process. ISD issues the food service permit only after this license. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 2 to 3 weeks; when a public hearing is needed, several weeks from filing to the hearing. https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScp721MuqsSIAPeryi7VN7cdMEH4cXgnY2MAze5iM3LSrDCcw/viewform?usp=sf_link
11. Site cleanliness license, City of Boston Inspectional Services. Listed with the Common Victualler License among the approvals Boston's restaurant guide asks for before the food service permit; it covers how the place keeps its trash and dumpsters. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/departments/inspectional-services
12. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Boston Inspectional Services. Required before opening; Boston's guide accepts a Certificate of Inspection (with the Fire Department's capacity approval) in its place. Either one must be in hand before the health inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov/departments/inspectional-services
13. Food service permit, City of Boston Inspectional Services, Health Division. Email the application (with its workers' comp affidavit), the EIN and the food protection manager certificate to ISDHealth@boston.gov, or bring them to 1010 Massachusetts Ave, 4th floor. Before the opening inspection, which you book a few days ahead, have the allergen certificate, Certificate of Occupancy, Common Victualler License and paid fees ready. Fee: Varies. Takes: 1 to 2 business days when the space isn't changing; after a build-out, the inspection is usually done within 1 business day of proof of every other approval. https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2026/07/%28English%29%20Food%20Establishment%20Permit%20Application%20updated-combined.pdf

Opening a cosmetics store in Boston takes 11 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the Certificate of Occupancy. The fixed government fees add up to about $565, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 7 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.

3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax registration, Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Register for sales tax and withholding before trading. Fee: Free. Takes: DOR doesn't publish how long registration takes; once approved, it mails a registration certificate for each location. https://mtc.dor.state.ma.us
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Boston business certificate (DBA), City of Boston, City Clerk. Needed when the business trades under a name other than its legal name. Bring the notarized form, the signed lease and photo ID to City Hall, Room 601 (the clerk notarizes free), or mail them with a check; there is no online filing. Employers who pay wages for work done in Massachusetts register with DUA online: open Unemployment Services for Employers without logging in and choose Register your Business. ### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Miami
https://www.placetta.com/guides/miami/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Miami takes 11 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/manage-business/efile/fictitious-name-registration/
5. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
6. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
7. Certificate of Occupancy or Completion after the build-out, City of Miami Building Department. A new building, or one that has undergone construction, shows its CO or CC to get the Certificate of Use. Fee: Varies. https://www.miami.gov/Business/New-Business-Guide
8. City of Miami CU (use approval), City of Miami, Office of Zoning. For a business opening or moving in the city, applied for online only through MiamiBiz once construction is done (with the certificate of occupancy or completion for new or renovated space). After the $50 fee, pass the DERM, fire and code inspections, plus Health or DBPR for food, within 90 working days of starting the application. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city contacts you within five business days of applying and paying. https://apps.miami.gov/MiamiBizIntake
9. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. Takes: Most applications are processed within a few business days; mailed ones take longer. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
10. City of Miami business tax receipt, City of Miami. Every business operating in the city needs one, after its Certificate of Use. Apply online with the EIN and, for a restaurant, the state food service license; the city emails an invoice, and the interim receipt comes by email once it's paid. A Miami-Dade County receipt is needed as well. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city doesn't publish how long approval takes; the interim receipt is emailed after payment. https://us.openforms.com/Form/98a6acf3-a616-4139-857d-68f4d9a4e51e
11. Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt, Miami-Dade County Tax Collector. Needed for each place of business in the county, and inside a city on top of the city's receipt. Apply online in BTExpress after completing the attestation that the business doesn't trade with Cuba in violation of federal law. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to three business days after the attestation for the receipt to be ready to print. https://county-taxes.net/fl-miamidade/btexpress
What's different for a milk tea shop in Miami:

Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration

7. Certificate of Occupancy or Completion after the build-out, City of Miami Building Department. A new building, or one that has undergone construction, shows its CO or CC to get the Certificate of Use. Fee: Varies. https://www.miami.gov/Business/New-Business-Guide
8. City of Miami CU (use approval), City of Miami, Office of Zoning. For a business opening or moving in the city, applied for online only through MiamiBiz once construction is done (with the certificate of occupancy or completion for new or renovated space). After the $50 fee, pass the DERM, fire and code inspections, plus Health or DBPR for food, within 90 working days of starting the application. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city contacts you within five business days of applying and paying. https://apps.miami.gov/MiamiBizIntake
9. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. 9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/manage-business/efile/fictitious-name-registration/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Miami CU (use approval), City of Miami, Office of Zoning. For a business opening or moving in the city, applied for online only through MiamiBiz once construction is done (with the certificate of occupancy or completion for new or renovated space). After the $50 fee, pass the DERM, fire and code inspections, plus Health or DBPR for food, within 90 working days of starting the application. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city contacts you within five business days of applying and paying. https://apps.miami.gov/MiamiBizIntake
10. City of Miami business tax receipt, City of Miami. Every business operating in the city needs one, after its Certificate of Use. Apply online with the EIN and, for a restaurant, the state food service license; the city emails an invoice, and the interim receipt comes by email once it's paid. A Miami-Dade County receipt is needed as well. Fee: Varies. Takes: The city doesn't publish how long approval takes; the interim receipt is emailed after payment. https://us.openforms.com/Form/98a6acf3-a616-4139-857d-68f4d9a4e51e
11. Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt, Miami-Dade County Tax Collector. Needed for each place of business in the county, and inside a city on top of the city's receipt. Apply online in BTExpress after completing the attestation that the business doesn't trade with Cuba in violation of federal law. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to three business days after the attestation for the receipt to be ready to print. https://county-taxes.net/fl-miamidade/btexpress

### Restaurants in Dallas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/dallas/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Dallas takes 14 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $1,567, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. Takes: Dallas's goal is to review a CO application within 15 business days on average, though its CO page notes processing times differ based on demand. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
9. Building permit for tenant finish-out, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow under Commercial Permits, upload the plans and checklists, and pay online. Fee: Varies. Takes: Dallas's goal for a commercial alteration/addition is an initial plan review within 15 business days and a resubmittal review within 7. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/pages/fees.aspx
10. Food establishment plan review, City of Dallas Planning and Development, Health Plan Review. Submit two sets of plans, equipment sheets, finishes and the menu at 320 E. Jefferson Blvd., where the plans are reviewed and stamped. Fee: $200. Takes: Dallas's goal for the Health team's initial plan review is 15 business days. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Health-Inspections.aspx
11. Food establishment permit, City of Dallas Code Compliance, Consumer Health. File CCS-FRM-424 with photo ID, the Texas sales tax permit and the fee, then book the health inspection. A registered food manager must be on site. Fee: $121. Takes: Consumer Health doesn't publish a processing time; after you apply, you schedule and coordinate the required health inspections with your permitting inspector. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/codecompliance/consumer-health/Pages/food-establishment.aspx
12. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $296. Takes: Typically about two business days if everything required is submitted. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
13. Kitchen hood fire-extinguishing system permit, Dallas Fire-Rescue. Get the application from Dallas Fire-Rescue, 1551 Baylor St., Suite 400. Fee: $250. Takes: Dallas doesn't publish a review time for kitchen hood fire-extinguishing system permits; its published goals cover only fire alarm, sprinkler and flammable-liquid reviews. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/fire-rescue/Pages/Prevention-and-Investigation-Bureau.aspx
14. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

What's different for a bakery in Dallas:
- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. Takes: Dallas's goal is to review a CO application within 15 business days on average, though its CO page notes processing times differ based on demand. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
10. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $296. Takes: Typically about two business days if everything required is submitted. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Importers and online sellers in Dallas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/dallas/importer-ecommerce.html
Opening an importer or e-commerce seller in Dallas takes 9 filings with 5 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 1 fee is set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Restaurants in Austin
https://www.placetta.com/guides/austin/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Austin takes 14 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $815, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. Takes: Change-of-use reviews now take about two weeks (three review disciplines since October 2025). https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
9. Building permit for a tenant finish-out, City of Austin Development Services. Apply with the city's commercial building permit web form (not AB+C) to build, alter or convert the space, with plans for commercial plan review. Fee: Varies. Takes: Commercial plan review for a remodel up to 25,000 sq ft takes 10 business days; small projects, such as a finish-out under 10,000 sq ft, take 5 business days. https://austintexas.jotform.com/austin-dsd/commercial-building-permit-web-form
10. Food establishment plan review, City of Austin Development Services, with Austin Public Health. For new construction or a remodel: inside the City of Austin, apply online through Development Services; in unincorporated Travis County, through Austin Public Health's My Health Department portal. Fee: $312. Takes: Inside the City of Austin, the food plan review is submitted with the commercial building application, whose review takes 10 business days for a remodel up to 25,000 sq ft (5 for small projects). https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
11. Pre-opening health inspection, Austin Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Apply on the My Health Department portal (Retail and Wholesale Food Applications, Pre-Opening Inspection), in person at 1520 Rutherford Ln, or by mail. Needed for a new place, a remodel or a change of owner; the place must pass before the permit is issued. Fee: $178. Takes: Austin Public Health doesn't publish how soon a pre-opening inspection happens; you apply once the space is built, and you must pass before the permit is issued. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
12. Food enterprise permit (fixed food establishment), Austin Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued after the pre-opening inspection passes. Apply on the My Health Department portal (Food Enterprise, Operational Permit Application) or in person at 1520 Rutherford Ln; the form says mailed applications are not accepted. A certified food manager must be on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin Public Health doesn't publish a processing time; the operating permit is issued after the pre-opening inspection is approved. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
13. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin doesn't publish a review time for sign permits; staff review the application once the review fee is paid and email you the decision. https://abc.austintexas.gov
14. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

What's different for a bakery in Austin:
- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. Takes: Change-of-use reviews now take about two weeks (three review disciplines since October 2025). https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
10. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: Austin doesn't publish a review time for sign permits; staff review the application once the review fee is paid and email you the decision. https://abc.austintexas.gov
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Restaurants in Washington, DC
https://www.placetta.com/guides/washington-dc/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Washington, DC takes 9 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the food services business license. The fixed government fees add up to about $99, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, Corporations Division. Form DLC-1 goes to the Superintendent of Corporations online, by mail or at the counter. Fee: Varies. https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1616716
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. DC tax registration, DC Office of Tax and Revenue. Register with the Office of Tax and Revenue on the FR-500. Every basic business license applicant must be registered and in good standing, and the license application checks the tax number for Clean Hands. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Office of Tax and Revenue may take up to 10 business days to process a new registration. https://mytax.dc.gov
4. DC certified food protection manager card, DC Health. A manager who passed a nationally recognized food safety exam applies for DC Health's ID card with a copy of the certificate, in person at 899 North Capitol Street NE or by mail. DLCP asks for the DC Health food manager's certificate with the food license, and a certified manager has to be on duty whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://doh.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/doh/publication/attachments/Application%20for%20ID%20Cards.pdf
5. Building permit, DC Department of Buildings. A change of use takes building permits and final inspections before the new Certificate of Occupancy. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf
6. Unemployment insurance employer registration, DC Department of Employment Services, UI Tax Division. Any business with employees working in DC registers online in the Employer Self-Service Portal, which also takes the wage reports and tax payments. Fee: Varies. https://essp.does.dc.gov
7. Food establishment plan review, DC Health, Food Safety and Hygiene Inspection Services Division. Needed before building, converting or remodeling a food establishment, or changing its type of food operation. Plans, specifications and the menu go to DC Health through ProjectDox with the building permit application. Fee: Varies. https://dchealth.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/doh/publication/attachments/FS%28redtop%29%20-%20Plan%20review%202018%20v2.pdf
8. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf
9. Food services business license, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, with DC Health. The basic business license for restaurants, delis, caterers and other food businesses. Apply online in BOSS with the Certificate of Occupancy, the DC Health food manager's certificate, the approved DC Health inspection report, tax registration and Clean Hands, and corporate registration if you have one; pick only the category the business was approved for. Fee: $99. Takes: DLCP doesn't publish a processing time; apply once DC Health has approved the inspection. https://boss.dc.gov
