8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Warehouses and 3PLs in Washington, DC
https://www.placetta.com/guides/washington-dc/warehouse-3pl.html
Opening a warehouse or 3PL in Washington, DC takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Certificate of Occupancy. None of them has a fixed government fee, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, Corporations Division. Form DLC-1 goes to the Superintendent of Corporations online, by mail or at the counter. Fee: Varies. https://dlcp.dc.gov/node/1616716
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Corporate registration and basic business license, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection. Register the company, then get the basic business license for the activity. Fee: Varies. Takes: DLCP doesn't publish how long a Basic Business License takes; you need a processed FR-500 tax registration and a Clean Hands check before you can apply. https://dlcp.dc.gov
4. DC tax registration, DC Office of Tax and Revenue. Register with the Office of Tax and Revenue on the FR-500. Every basic business license applicant must be registered and in good standing, and the license application checks the tax number for Clean Hands. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Office of Tax and Revenue may take up to 10 business days to process a new registration. https://mytax.dc.gov
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
9. Unemployment insurance employer registration, DC Department of Employment Services, UI Tax Division. Any business with employees working in DC registers online in the Employer Self-Service Portal, which also takes the wage reports and tax payments. Fee: Varies. https://essp.does.dc.gov
10. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf

### Restaurants in Atlanta
https://www.placetta.com/guides/atlanta/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Atlanta takes 9 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food service permit. None of them has a fixed government fee, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ecorp.sos.ga.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Sales tax registration, Georgia Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax online. Fee: Free. Takes: After registering online in the Georgia Tax Center, you should get your tax account number by email within 15 minutes. https://gtc.dor.ga.gov
4. Certified food safety manager, Georgia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. At least one employee with supervisory and management duties passes an accredited food safety manager exam, and is designated to this one place only. A new food service establishment has 60 days from its permit to employ one, and tells the county within 30 days if it loses its manager. Fee: Varies. https://dph.georgia.gov/node/146
5. Building permit for the build-out, City of Atlanta, Office of Buildings. The Office of Buildings issues the permits construction and alteration need under the Atlanta Municipal Code, and inspects the work. Fee: Varies. https://atlantaga.gov/home/showdocument?id=19215
6. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. Takes: Atlanta doesn't publish how long a new license takes; the zoning review is done inside the city as part of the application. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/
7. Food service plan review, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Before building or extensively remodeling, mail or bring the application, scaled plans, equipment specifications and the fee to the Environmental Health district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County applies to the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: The county doesn't publish a review time; Georgia's food service rules ask for plans at least 14 business days before construction starts. https://FultonCountyGa.gov/-/media/Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection/Link-List-Items/Food-Service-Application.pdf
8. Unemployment insurance tax account (DOL-1A), Georgia Department of Labor. Employers with a quarterly payroll of $1,500, or a worker in 20 weeks of a year, file Form DOL-1A and then quarterly tax and wage reports. Fee: Free. https://dol.georgia.gov/node/2291
9. Food service permit, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued by the county once the application and fee are in, the plans are approved and the place passes its pre-opening inspection; apply by mail or in person at the district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County gets its permit from the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Georgia's food service rules ask for the permit application at least 10 business days before opening. https://fultoncountyga.gov/Inside-Fulton-County/Fulton-County-Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection

What's different for a bakery in Atlanta:
- The Georgia Department of Agriculture regulates bakeries as food retailers, while restaurants get their food service permit from the county health department (Fulton County in Atlanta). Odelia confirms which licenses yours, by what it sells and where it's eaten. Georgia Department of Agriculture: "regulates and monitors food retailers: grocery stores, convenience stores, bakeries, seafood operations, salvage food operations, mobile meat trucks, and rolling stores." https://agr.ga.gov/retailers (read 2026-10-21)

### Restaurants in Philadelphia
https://www.placetta.com/guides/philadelphia/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Philadelphia takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food preparation and serving license. The fixed government fees add up to about $155, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation, Pennsylvania Department of State. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://file.dos.pa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Pennsylvania tax registration (sales tax license and employer accounts), Pennsylvania Department of Revenue. Register in myPATH (new customers don't need to log in) for sales, use and hotel occupancy tax, employer withholding and unemployment compensation. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Department of Revenue doesn't publish how long myPATH registration takes to issue a sales tax license. https://mypath.pa.gov/_/
4. Philadelphia food safety certificate, Philadelphia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Every food business has at least one person certified in food safety at all times. Take a food manager safety course with an approved provider, send the training certificate to the Health Department for checking, then apply for the city certificate online, or in person or by mail with a money order. Fee: $30. Takes: Checking the training certificate takes up to 10 business days, and the certificate itself up to 30 business days. https://philadph.formstack.com/forms/fscapp
5. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
6. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. Takes: Issued automatically online, or while you wait in person. https://eclipse.phila.gov/
7. Food business plan review, Philadelphia Department of Public Health, Office of Food Protection. Anyone opening a stationary food business applies after zoning is approved and before construction or installing food equipment. Call 215-685-7495 to submit, book an appointment or walk in at 7801 Essington Ave (weekdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.). The application covers 13 items, from the site plan to the menu, with a copy of the city food safety certificate. Fee: Varies. Takes: A worksheet and fee letter within 30 business days; after you return them, the Health Department replies within 30 business days. Expedited review takes 10 business days. https://phila.gov/media/20250423122123/Plan-Review-for-Stationary-Food-Businesses-2025-fillable.pdf
8. Building permit for the build-out, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Construction or alterations to the space need a building permit from L&I's Building Unit, filed in eCLIPSE; signs and emission-producing equipment have their own permits. Fee: Varies. https://eclipse.phila.gov/
9. Food preparation and serving license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. For any business that prepares or serves food to the public. Apply in eCLIPSE with the BIRT ID, the Commercial Activity License, proof of occupancy (a license for the same use in the last 3 years, or zoning approval) and the Health Department's License Eligibility Report dated within 30 days. Fee: Varies. Takes: Online applications are reviewed within 5 business days. https://eclipse.phila.gov/

### Grocery stores in Philadelphia
https://www.placetta.com/guides/philadelphia/grocery-store.html
Opening a grocery store in Philadelphia takes 7 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the food preparation and serving license. The fixed government fees add up to about $155, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Pennsylvania Department of State. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://file.dos.pa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Pennsylvania tax registration (sales tax license and employer accounts), Pennsylvania Department of Revenue. Register in myPATH (new customers don't need to log in) for sales, use and hotel occupancy tax, employer withholding and unemployment compensation. Fee: Varies. Takes: The Department of Revenue doesn't publish how long myPATH registration takes to issue a sales tax license. https://mypath.pa.gov/_/
4. Philadelphia food safety certificate, Philadelphia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Every food business has at least one person certified in food safety at all times. Take a food manager safety course with an approved provider, send the training certificate to the Health Department for checking, then apply for the city certificate online, or in person or by mail with a money order. Fee: $30. Takes: Checking the training certificate takes up to 10 business days, and the certificate itself up to 30 business days. https://philadph.formstack.com/forms/fscapp
5. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
6. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. Takes: Issued automatically online, or while you wait in person. https://eclipse.phila.gov/
7. Food preparation and serving license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. For any business that prepares or serves food to the public. Apply in eCLIPSE with the BIRT ID, the Commercial Activity License, proof of occupancy (a license for the same use in the last 3 years, or zoning approval) and the Health Department's License Eligibility Report dated within 30 days. Fee: Varies. Takes: Online applications are reviewed within 5 business days. https://eclipse.phila.gov/

### Cosmetics stores in Philadelphia
https://www.placetta.com/guides/philadelphia/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Philadelphia takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the commercial activity license. The fixed government fees add up to about $125, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Pennsylvania Department of State. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://file.dos.pa.gov

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Takes: The Department of Revenue doesn't publish how long myPATH registration takes to issue a sales tax license. https://mypath.pa.gov/_/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. Takes: Issued automatically online, or while you wait in person. https://eclipse.phila.gov/

### Restaurants in Las Vegas
https://www.placetta.com/guides/las-vegas/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Las Vegas takes 10 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and state business license and ending with the food establishment health permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $35, 7 fees are set by the space or the business and 1 filing is free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation and state business license, Nevada Secretary of State (SilverFlume). Form the company and get the state business license together online. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Nevada state business license, Nevada Secretary of State. Every business that conducts business in Nevada holds the Secretary of State's business license (or a certificate of exemption), on top of any city or county license. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov/
4. Nevada sales tax permit, Nevada Department of Taxation. Register online in My Nevada Tax once you have an EIN and the state business license, or mail the Nevada Business Registration Form. Businesses paying more than $50,000 in wages in a quarter also register for the Modified Business Tax, through DETR. Fee: $15. Takes: Online, the permit number comes within 24 hours; by mail, several weeks. https://mynvtax.nv.gov/tap/_/
5. Certified food safety manager, Southern Nevada Health District. The Health District's permit application asks for a person in charge who is a Certified Food Safety Manager, with a copy of the certificate attached. The certificate comes from an accredited food protection manager exam. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf
6. Food handler cards for staff, Southern Nevada Health District. Everyone employed in or running a food establishment holds one. A first card means an in-person test at a Health District location with photo ID; some renewals can be done online. A Certified Food Safety Manager card also meets the requirement. Fee: $20. https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/?p=3661
7. City of Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. For an address inside City of Las Vegas limits; check the jurisdiction first, since other addresses license with Clark County or their own city. Confirm the zoning allows the business and the building is code compliant, get the state business license and register with the Department of Taxation, then apply on the city's online portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: A license technician emails within 5 business days; the license is issued within 30 days of applying, usually sooner. https://www.lasvegasnevada.gov/dashboard
8. Unemployment insurance employer account, Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation, Employment Security Division. Employers open their unemployment insurance account with DETR's Employment Security Division, whose Registration Unit handles Nevada business registration; DETR shares the details with the Department of Taxation. The account is then managed in the Employer Self-Service portal. Fee: Varies. http://nui.nv.gov/ess
9. Food establishment plan review, Southern Nevada Health District. Plans are needed for new and remodeled places and must be approved before construction starts. Email the application packet, plans in PDF, the menu, the food questionnaire and proof of the lease or deed to FOODREV@SNHD.ORG; a remote plan review follows and the invoice comes by email. Two construction walkthroughs are included. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf
10. Food establishment health permit, Southern Nevada Health District. Issued after the final permitting inspection, which needs a Certificate of Occupancy (or a temporary one) after new construction or a remodel, and every fee paid first. Food can't be stocked until the permit is approved. Fee: Varies. Takes: Inspection appointments can be up to 4 weeks out at busy times. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf

The fixed government fees add up to about $15, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation and state business license, Nevada Secretary of State (SilverFlume). Form the company and get the state business license together online. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Nevada state business license, Nevada Secretary of State. Every business that conducts business in Nevada holds the Secretary of State's business license (or a certificate of exemption), on top of any city or county license. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov/
4. Nevada sales tax permit, Nevada Department of Taxation. Register online in My Nevada Tax once you have an EIN and the state business license, or mail the Nevada Business Registration Form. Businesses paying more than $50,000 in wages in a quarter also register for the Modified Business Tax, through DETR. Fee: $15. Takes: Online, the permit number comes within 24 hours; by mail, several weeks. https://mynvtax.nv.gov/tap/_/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. City of Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. For an address inside City of Las Vegas limits; check the jurisdiction first, since other addresses license with Clark County or their own city. Confirm the zoning allows the business and the building is code compliant, get the state business license and register with the Department of Taxation, then apply on the city's online portal. Fee: Varies. Takes: A license technician emails within 5 business days; the license is issued within 30 days of applying, usually sooner. https://www.lasvegasnevada.gov/dashboard
11. Unemployment insurance employer account, Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation, Employment Security Division. Employers open their unemployment insurance account with DETR's Employment Security Division, whose Registration Unit handles Nevada business registration; DETR shares the details with the Department of Taxation. The account is then managed in the Employer Self-Service portal. Fee: Varies. http://nui.nv.gov/ess

### Restaurants in San Antonio
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-antonio/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in San Antonio takes 10 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants and dessert shops.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. Takes: DSHS doesn't issue the certificate itself; the accredited exam provider issues it as soon as you pass the exam. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. Takes: Each food employee must complete an accredited food handler course within 30 days of being hired; the training provider issues the card. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Antonio doesn't publish a processing time for a Certificate of Occupancy; for new construction it's issued once all required inspections are complete. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
9. Food establishment license, San Antonio Metropolitan Health District (Metro Health). Once the space is zoned for the use and the Certificate of Occupancy requirements are complete, buy the license at the Development and Business Services Center, 1901 S. Alamo. Fee: Varies. Takes: Metro Health doesn't publish a processing time; the license is issued only after all building, health and fire inspections are approved and recorded, and you must show a valid CofO to buy the permit. https://www.sanantonio.gov/Health/FoodLicensing/FAQs
10. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

What's different for a bakery in San Antonio:
- Texas requires a Food Manufacturer license from the Department of State Health Services (DSHS) of a business that packages food for wholesale or for a self-service display, and lists bakeries among its examples. It applies if the bakery packages its goods that way. Texas Department of State Health Services: "Processing and/or packaging any food product, including dietary supplements, ice, and water, for wholesale distribution or for sale via retail customer self-service." https://dshs.texas.gov/foods/manufacturers.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

Opening a toy store in San Antonio takes 10 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC) and ending with the franchise tax annual report. The fixed government fees add up to about $325, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. Takes: No standard time published; paid expedited service typically takes 2 to 3 business days. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. Takes: Account number issued instantly online. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Antonio doesn't publish a processing time for a Certificate of Occupancy; for new construction it's issued once all required inspections are complete. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
10. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. Takes: The Comptroller doesn't publish a processing time for the report; the annual franchise tax report is due May 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Tampa
https://www.placetta.com/guides/tampa/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in Tampa takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the florida public food service license. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/manage-business/efile/fictitious-name-registration/
5. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
6. Hillsborough County local business tax receipt, Hillsborough County Tax Collector. Get it before you start trading: apply online in BTExpress in one sitting, with the business name, SSN or EIN, a physical county address and any state or county license the business needs. Fee: Varies. Takes: Reviewed in 3 to 5 business days, then paid and printed online. https://www.hillstaxfl.gov/taxes/business-tax-services/new-regulated-businesses/
7. City of Tampa business tax receipt, City of Tampa Business Tax. A business inside Tampa city limits files the new business application online; the city may inspect the site. Fee: Varies. Takes: Tampa doesn't publish a processing time for a new business tax receipt; applications are made online or by appointment. https://www.tampa.gov/service/new-business-tax-receipt-application
8. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
9. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. Takes: Most applications are processed within a few business days; mailed ones take longer. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
What's different for a milk tea shop in Tampa:
- Florida's Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) permits coffee shops and juice and smoothie bars, and DBPR licenses restaurants and fast food. Neither names tea shops, so Odelia confirms which one licenses yours before anything is filed. Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: "These food establishments may include supermarkets, grocery stores, convenience stores, coffee shops, bakeries, retail meat markets, retail seafood markets, juice and smoothie bars," https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Food/Food-Establishments/Retail-Food-Establishment-Permit (read 2026-10-21)

https://www.placetta.com/guides/tampa/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Tampa takes 11 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the City of Tampa business tax receipt. The fixed government fees add up to about $175, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/manage-business/efile/fictitious-name-registration/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Hillsborough County local business tax receipt, Hillsborough County Tax Collector. Get it before you start trading: apply online in BTExpress in one sitting, with the business name, SSN or EIN, a physical county address and any state or county license the business needs. Fee: Varies. Takes: Reviewed in 3 to 5 business days, then paid and printed online. https://www.hillstaxfl.gov/taxes/business-tax-services/new-regulated-businesses/
11. City of Tampa business tax receipt, City of Tampa Business Tax. A business inside Tampa city limits files the new business application online; the city may inspect the site. Fee: Varies. Takes: Tampa doesn't publish a processing time for a new business tax receipt; applications are made online or by appointment. https://www.tampa.gov/service/new-business-tax-receipt-application

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Diego
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-diego/milk-tea-shop.html
Opening a milk tea shop in San Diego takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to coffee shops.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. City of San Diego Business Tax Certificate, City of San Diego, Office of the City Treasurer. Every business operating in the City of San Diego registers, online on the Treasurer's portal, by mail or in person by appointment. Late fees apply to applications received 15 days after the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to two weeks to receive the certificate. https://pay.sandiego.gov/BTaxApp
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality. Submit at least three sets of plans with the application and fee to a DEHQ office; plans are approved before the building permit is issued. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plans are approved or rejected within 20 working days of receipt. https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/deh/fhd/food/food_faq.html
10. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Diego Development Services. Issued after the final inspection of building permit work. Needed for a change of occupancy classification or a tenant improvement in a shell building; not needed for a change of owner or tenant when the occupancy doesn't change. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Diego doesn't publish a delivery time for a commercial Certificate of Occupancy; it's issued once every inspection under the permit has final approval (only affordable housing and shelters get set deadlines). https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletin/585
11. Public health permit (food facility), County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality. Required by law for every retail food facility in San Diego County. Fee: Varies. Takes: Plans are approved or rejected within 20 working days of receipt, and plan check staff issue the health permit when the facility passes its final inspection. https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/deh/fhd/food/food_faq.html
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a milk tea shop in San Diego:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)

California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

### Retail stores in San Diego
https://www.placetta.com/guides/san-diego/retail-store.html
Opening a retail store in San Diego takes 9 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the proposition 65 warning labels. The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 2 fees are set by the space or the business and 4 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to grocery stores.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. City of San Diego Business Tax Certificate, City of San Diego, Office of the City Treasurer. Every business operating in the City of San Diego registers, online on the Treasurer's portal, by mail or in person by appointment. Late fees apply to applications received 15 days after the business start date. Fee: Varies. Takes: Allow up to two weeks to receive the certificate. https://pay.sandiego.gov/BTaxApp
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Diego Development Services. Issued after the final inspection of building permit work. Needed for a change of occupancy classification or a tenant improvement in a shell building; not needed for a change of owner or tenant when the occupancy doesn't change. Fee: Varies. Takes: San Diego doesn't publish a delivery time for a commercial Certificate of Occupancy; it's issued once every inspection under the permit has final approval (only affordable housing and shelters get set deadlines). https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletin/585
8. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
9. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Irvine, Building Permits and Inspections. The plans and the permit application go in electronically through the city's IrvineReady! portal; the city inspects the work. Fee: Varies. https://cityofirvine.gov/node/69516
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Submit the plan check online with three sets of plans and specifications before construction; the fee is set at conditional approval. Fee: Varies. Takes: The initial plan review usually takes 20 working days. https://www.ochealthinfo.com/services-programs/environmental-health/plan-check
10. Food facility health permit, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Every food facility that stores, prepares, packages, serves or vends food needs a valid health permit; book inspections 5 working days ahead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Initial plan review usually takes 20 working days; inspections must be requested 5 working days ahead, and the health permit is issued once the final inspection passes. https://ochealthinfo.com/sites/healthcare/files/2023-04/Food%20Health%20Permit%20Application%20W.pdf
11. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. Takes: Irvine doesn't publish how long it takes to issue the license; the online application takes minutes, and new businesses must apply within 60 days of starting to avoid late fees. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)

A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113947.1
6. Food handler cards for staff, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. Every employee who prepares, stores or handles food gets a California Food Handler Card from an accredited course within 30 days of hire; the card is good for 3 years. Anyone holding a valid food manager certificate is exempt. Fee: Varies. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=113948
7. Building permit for the tenant improvement, City of Irvine, Building Permits and Inspections. The plans and the permit application go in electronically through the city's IrvineReady! portal; the city inspects the work. Fee: Varies. https://cityofirvine.gov/node/69516
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Submit the plan check online with three sets of plans and specifications before construction; the fee is set at conditional approval. Fee: Varies. Takes: The initial plan review usually takes 20 working days. https://www.ochealthinfo.com/services-programs/environmental-health/plan-check
10. Food facility health permit, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Every food facility that stores, prepares, packages, serves or vends food needs a valid health permit; book inspections 5 working days ahead. Fee: Varies. Takes: Initial plan review usually takes 20 working days; inspections must be requested 5 working days ahead, and the health permit is issued once the final inspection passes. https://ochealthinfo.com/sites/healthcare/files/2023-04/Food%20Health%20Permit%20Application%20W.pdf
11. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. Takes: Irvine doesn't publish how long it takes to issue the license; the online application takes minutes, and new businesses must apply within 60 days of starting to avoid late fees. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Bakeries in Irvine
https://www.placetta.com/guides/irvine/bakery.html
Opening a bakery in Irvine takes 12 filings with 9 agencies, starting with the Articles of Organization (California LLC) and ending with the LLC annual tax ($800). The fixed government fees add up to about $890, 6 fees are set by the space or the business and 3 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. Takes: Online filings are currently reviewed about 3 days after receipt (mail about 8 days), per the Oct 8, 2026 queue. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
2. Statement of Information (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Due within 90 days of forming or registering the LLC in California, then every two years. Filed in bizfile Online, or on the paper form by mail. Fee: $20. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
5. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. 8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. Food facility plan check, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Submit the plan check online with three sets of plans and specifications before construction; the fee is set at conditional approval. Fee: Varies. Takes: The initial plan review usually takes 20 working days. https://www.ochealthinfo.com/services-programs/environmental-health/plan-check
10. Food facility health permit, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. 11. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. Takes: Irvine doesn't publish how long it takes to issue the license; the online application takes minutes, and new businesses must apply within 60 days of starting to avoid late fees. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
What's different for a bakery in Irvine:
- Under California's food code, a food facility in a building built after January 1, 2004 that gives customers space to eat or drink on the premises must provide clean restrooms for them. The rule turns on that space, so whether to add seats is a build-out decision. California Retail Food Code, as Los Angeles County's construction guide states it: "that provides space for the consumption of food on the premises shall provide clean toilet facilities in good repair for consumers" https://admin.publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/inspection/construction-requirements-retail-food-facilities.htm (read 2026-10-21)
- California's Processed Food Registration, from the Department of Public Health, covers bakery products. A retail food facility that sells directly to consumers under a county health permit is exempt, so a bakery selling only over its own counter doesn't need it; making goods for other stores or cafes falls outside that exemption. California Department of Public Health: "General foods such as bakery products, noodles, seafood (except molluscan shellfish)" https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DFDCS/Pages/FDBPrograms/FoodSafetyProgram/PFRFAQs.aspx (read 2026-10-21)

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
4. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. Takes: Often issued the same day. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/

7. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
8. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. Takes: Mail-in registration takes about 10 to 14 days; online is faster. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/

12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. Takes: Paying the $800 LLC tax online through Web Pay is immediate; it's due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the LLC's tax year. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
13. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
14. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. Takes: Nothing is filed with or approved by OEHHA, so there's no processing time; the business decides whether a warning is needed and must have it in place itself. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. Takes: After registering online, the certificate number is available on the website after three business days. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Registration of a fictitious name (DBA), Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations. Needed before doing business under any name other than the legal name. Advertise the name once in a newspaper in the county, then register online at Sunbiz or mail the form with the fee. Fee: $50. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/manage-business/efile/fictitious-name-registration/
5. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
6. City of Orlando business tax receipt and certificate of use, City of Orlando, Permitting Services. Businesses inside city limits apply online with the Sunbiz registration, EIN and any state license; the certificate of use confirms the zoning allows the business. Get it before the county receipt. Fee: Varies. Takes: A billing summary within 10 business days of processing; the receipt is mailed after payment. https://orlando.opencounter.com/permits/business-tax-receipt
7. Orange County (FL) local business tax receipt, Orange County Tax Collector. Apply online or in person after the city receipt, uploading the city receipt, Sunbiz registration, any state license and the EIN. Fee: Varies. Takes: Orange County doesn't publish a processing time; Zoning must approve the business (and a CO is needed for new or altered space) before the Tax Collector issues the receipt. https://county-taxes.net/fl-orange/btexpress
8. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
9. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. Takes: Most applications are processed within a few business days; mailed ones take longer. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
What's different for a milk tea shop in Orlando:
- Florida's Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) permits coffee shops and juice and smoothie bars, and DBPR licenses restaurants and fast food. Neither names tea shops, so Odelia confirms which one licenses yours before anything is filed. Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: "These food establishments may include supermarkets, grocery stores, convenience stores, coffee shops, bakeries, retail meat markets, retail seafood markets, juice and smoothie bars," https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Food/Food-Establishments/Retail-Food-Establishment-Permit (read 2026-10-21)
