### Cosmetics stores in Bellevue
https://www.placetta.com/guides/bellevue/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Bellevue takes 9 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation and ending with the City of Bellevue business license. The fixed government fees add up to about $119, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 5 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation, Washington Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the company or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ccfs.sos.wa.gov
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Washington business license (state tax registration), Washington Department of Revenue, Business Licensing Service. File online in My DOR, or by mail. It gives the business its UBI number and tax registration, registers trade names and city and state endorsements, and passes your details to Employment Security and Labor and Industries, which open the unemployment insurance and workers' comp accounts. Fee: Varies. Takes: About 10 business days; city or state endorsements can add another 2 to 3 weeks. https://secure.dor.wa.gov/home
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Bellevue business license, City of Bellevue Finance, Tax Division. Needed once Bellevue gross receipts reach $4,000 a year (or for a regulated activity), after the Washington business license; apply through FileLocal. It doesn't expire, but tax returns are due on the assigned schedule. Fee: $119. https://www.filelocal-wa.gov/Default_FileLocal.aspx

### Restaurants in Rockville
https://www.placetta.com/guides/rockville/restaurant.html
Opening a restaurant in Rockville takes 8 filings with 6 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Montgomery County food service facility license. The fixed government fees add up to about $100, 5 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top. The same filings apply to milk tea and bubble tea shops, coffee shops, hot pot restaurants, bakeries and dessert shops.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). File online in Maryland Business Express, or mail the signed Articles with a $100 check to SDAT's Charter Division in Baltimore. The resident agent signs too. Fee: $100. Takes: Standard review takes 6 to 8 weeks. https://egov.maryland.gov/businessexpress
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Maryland sales and use tax, withholding and unemployment insurance registration, Comptroller of Maryland, Central Registration. One application opens the sales and use tax license, employer withholding and the unemployment insurance account: online, by fax (410-260-7908) or by mail to Central Registration in Annapolis. Fee: Free. https://interactive.marylandtaxes.gov/webapps/comptrollercra/entrance.asp
4. Certified food service manager, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services. The facility must be under the immediate control of a Certified Food Service Manager, licensed by the county. Fee: Varies. https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/HHS-Special/LandRLicenseFoodService.html
5. Food service plan review, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, Licensure & Regulatory Services. Health and Human Services reviews the plans of any place that sells or prepares food before a building permit issues. The plans go in with the building permit to the office for the address: the county's Department of Permitting Services (restaurant interior alteration permit), or the City of Rockville's or Gaithersburg's own permitting office. Fee: Varies. https://montgomerycountymd.gov/HHS/Resources/Files/L%26R/Guidance%20-%20DHHS%20Plan%20Review%20via%20DPS%2010_2024.pdf
6. Commercial occupancy permit, City of Rockville Inspection Services. A commercial tenant applies through MGO Connect; the city inspects before the permit issues. Fee: Varies. https://www.rockvillemd.gov/mgoconnect
7. Building permit for the build-out, City of Rockville Inspection Services. Apply through MGO Connect before construction; most permits need inspections before the work is final. Fee: Varies. https://www.rockvillemd.gov/mgoconnect
8. Montgomery County food service facility license, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, Licensure & Regulatory Services. A license is needed before opening: apply and pay on the county's CivicGov portal, or mail or fax the application to Licensure & Regulatory Services in Wheaton. The county answers in 10 to 14 business days and mails the license. Fee: Varies. https://www.civicgov4.com/md_montgomery/portal/

### Grocery stores in Rockville
https://www.placetta.com/guides/rockville/grocery-store.html
Opening a grocery store in Rockville takes 7 filings with 7 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the Montgomery County food service facility license. The fixed government fees add up to about $100, 4 fees are set by the space or the business and 2 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). File online in Maryland Business Express, or mail the signed Articles with a $100 check to SDAT's Charter Division in Baltimore. The resident agent signs too. Fee: $100. Takes: Standard review takes 6 to 8 weeks. https://egov.maryland.gov/businessexpress
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Maryland sales and use tax, withholding and unemployment insurance registration, Comptroller of Maryland, Central Registration. One application opens the sales and use tax license, employer withholding and the unemployment insurance account: online, by fax (410-260-7908) or by mail to Central Registration in Annapolis. Fee: Free. https://interactive.marylandtaxes.gov/webapps/comptrollercra/entrance.asp
4. Certified food service manager, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services. The facility must be under the immediate control of a Certified Food Service Manager, licensed by the county. Fee: Varies. https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/HHS-Special/LandRLicenseFoodService.html
5. Trader's license, Clerk of the Circuit Court (your county). Anyone who sells goods in Maryland, other than a grower or manufacturer, gets this from the county's Circuit Court clerk before selling, after opening a sales tax account and registering the entity with SDAT. Fee: Varies. https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/businesses/new-business/business-licenses.html
6. Commercial occupancy permit, City of Rockville Inspection Services. A commercial tenant applies through MGO Connect; the city inspects before the permit issues. Fee: Varies. https://www.rockvillemd.gov/mgoconnect
7. Montgomery County food service facility license, Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, Licensure & Regulatory Services. A license is needed before opening: apply and pay on the county's CivicGov portal, or mail or fax the application to Licensure & Regulatory Services in Wheaton. The county answers in 10 to 14 business days and mails the license. Fee: Varies. https://www.civicgov4.com/md_montgomery/portal/

### Cosmetics stores in Rockville
https://www.placetta.com/guides/rockville/cosmetics-store.html
Opening a cosmetics store in Rockville takes 10 filings with 8 agencies, starting with the LLC formation (Articles of Organization) and ending with the commercial occupancy permit. The fixed government fees add up to about $100, 3 fees are set by the space or the business and 6 filings are free. Build-out, insurance and adviser costs are on top.
1. LLC formation (Articles of Organization), Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). File online in Maryland Business Express, or mail the signed Articles with a $100 check to SDAT's Charter Division in Baltimore. The resident agent signs too. Fee: $100. Takes: Standard review takes 6 to 8 weeks. https://egov.maryland.gov/businessexpress
2. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. Takes: Fax: about 4 business days. Mail: about 4 to 5 weeks. Phone: issued on the call. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
3. Maryland sales and use tax, withholding and unemployment insurance registration, Comptroller of Maryland, Central Registration. One application opens the sales and use tax license, employer withholding and the unemployment insurance account: online, by fax (410-260-7908) or by mail to Central Registration in Annapolis. Fee: Free. https://interactive.marylandtaxes.gov/webapps/comptrollercra/entrance.asp
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. Takes: Up to 5 business days. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. Takes: At least 5 business days for review. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Trader's license, Clerk of the Circuit Court (your county). Anyone who sells goods in Maryland, other than a grower or manufacturer, gets this from the county's Circuit Court clerk before selling, after opening a sales tax account and registering the entity with SDAT. Fee: Varies. https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/businesses/new-business/business-licenses.html
10. Commercial occupancy permit, City of Rockville Inspection Services. A commercial tenant applies through MGO Connect; the city inspects before the permit issues. Fee: Varies. https://www.rockvillemd.gov/mgoconnect
